description: S-024: GPU Execution for Solar Host Step Containers — structured GpuOptions model, NVIDIA Container Toolkit detection, GPU inventory and pre-flight validation, NVIDIA environment passthrough, tests, and documentation.

userStories.title: GPU error types
userStories.description: As a developer, I need distinct GPU errors in the Docker and jobs layers so callers get clear failures when the toolkit is missing or requested GPUs are invalid.
acceptanceCriteria: Add GpuUnavailableError to solar_host/docker/errors.py (subclass of DockerServiceError) with message indicating NVIDIA Container Toolkit is not available
Export GpuUnavailableError from solar_host/docker/__init__.py
Add GpuValidationError to solar_host/jobs/errors.py for invalid device IDs or count exceeding host inventory
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: GpuOptions model and StepDefinition migration
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a structured GpuOptions model on step definitions so SuperNova and the executor can express explicit GPU count or device pinning instead of a boolean flag.
acceptanceCriteria: Add GpuOptions Pydantic model to solar_host/jobs/models.py with count: int | None and device_ids: list[str] | None
Add @model_validator requiring at least one of count or device_ids; empty gpu: {} raises ValidationError at parse time
Do not silently default count to -1 when both fields are absent
Replace StepDefinition.gpu: bool = False with gpu: GpuOptions | None = None (null means no GPU)
Document semantics: gpu: {"count": -1} for all GPUs (explicit replacement for legacy gpu: true), gpu: {"count": 1} for one GPU, gpu: {"device_ids": ["0"]} for pinned devices
Export GpuOptions from solar_host/jobs/__init__.py
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: DockerService NVIDIA toolkit and DeviceRequest wiring
userStories.description: As a developer, I need DockerService to probe for the nvidia runtime and build DeviceRequest objects from GpuOptions before creating step containers.
acceptanceCriteria: Add is_nvidia_toolkit_available() to solar_host/docker/service.py: return True when "nvidia" is in client.info()["Runtimes"], False on exception or missing runtime
Change create_container gpu parameter from bool to gpu: GpuOptions | None = None
When gpu is None: no device_requests (unchanged non-GPU behaviour)
When gpu is set and toolkit unavailable: raise GpuUnavailableError
When gpu.device_ids is set: DeviceRequest(device_ids=..., capabilities=[["gpu"]])
When gpu.device_ids is None: DeviceRequest(count=gpu.count, capabilities=[["gpu"]]) — count guaranteed by GpuOptions validator
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: GPU device inventory
userStories.description: As a developer, I need per-device GPU inventory from pynvml so pre-flight validation can compare requested devices and counts against the host.
acceptanceCriteria: Add get_gpu_devices() to solar_host/memory_monitor.py returning list[dict[str, object]]
Each entry includes index (int), uuid (str), name (str), total_gb (float), used_gb (float)
Return empty list when pynvml is unavailable or no GPUs are detected
Reuse existing pynvml import pattern from _get_nvidia_memory()
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: JobStepExecutor GPU validation and NVIDIA env passthrough
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the step executor to validate GPU options against host inventory and pass standard NVIDIA container environment variables when a step requests GPU execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Add _validate_gpu_options(self, gpu: GpuOptions) to solar_host/jobs/step_executor.py
When get_gpu_devices() returns inventory: reject device_ids not matching available UUIDs or string indices; reject gpu.count > available_count when count != -1
When inventory is empty: skip validation silently (runtime will fail if misconfigured)
Call _validate_gpu_options before create_container in run()
Update create_container call to pass step_def.gpu (GpuOptions | None) instead of bool
In build_environment: when step_def.gpu is not None, setdefault NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=all and NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility before step_def.environment merge so callers can override
Propagate GpuUnavailableError from Docker layer as step failure
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Unit tests for GPU execution
userStories.description: As a developer, I need unit tests covering toolkit detection, GpuOptions validation, container GPU wiring, executor pre-flight checks, and NVIDIA environment variables.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/test_job_models.py: GpuOptions with count, device_ids, and both; GpuOptions() with neither field raises ValidationError; StepDefinition accepts gpu: GpuOptions | None

tests/test_docker_service.py: is_nvidia_toolkit_available when nvidia present, absent, and on exception; create_container with GpuOptions(count=2), GpuOptions(count=-1), GpuOptions(device_ids=["0","1"]), gpu=None (no device requests); GpuUnavailableError when toolkit missing
tests/test_job_step_executor.py: _validate_gpu_options valid/invalid device IDs and count exceeding inventory; GpuUnavailableError propagation; build_environment includes NVIDIA vars when gpu is set
All tests pass

userStories.title: GPU execution documentation
userStories.description: As an operator, I need README guidance and example job JSON so I can verify NVIDIA Container Toolkit integration on GPU hosts outside CI.
acceptanceCriteria: Add GPU Execution section to host/README.md
Document manual verification: docker run --rm --gpus '"device=0"' nvidia/cuda:12.0-base nvidia-smi
Include example job JSON snippets: gpu: {"device_ids": ["0"]}, gpu: {"count": 1}, gpu: {"count": -1} as explicit replacement for legacy gpu: true
Note recommended default gpu: {"count": 1} on multi-GPU hosts
